hints: Look at the scale bar labelled 5 µm under the mesophyll photo. Measure how long that bar is on your paper with a ruler in mm, that is your image size.
Remember magnification = image size divided by actual size, and you must get both in the same units first using 1 mm = 1000 µm.
walkthrough:
**Measure the image size**

Grab a ruler and measure the printed 5 µm scale bar. On the exam paper it is about 14 mm long.

That 14 mm is the image size.

**Convert to the same units**

The actual size is 5 µm, so convert your measurement from mm to µm.

Key conversion:
$$1 \text{ mm} = 1000 \text{ } \mu\text{m}$$
$$14 \text{ mm} = 14 \times 1000 = 14000 \text{ } \mu\text{m}$$

**Calculate magnification**

Now apply the magic triangle formula.

Key calculation:
$$\text{magnification} = \frac{\text{image size}}{\text{actual size}} = \frac{14000}{5} = 2800$$
So the photomicrograph is at x2800.

options.A: Too small by a factor of 10, usually from a unit conversion slip when changing mm to µm.
options.B: Correct, a 14 mm image of a 5 µm bar gives 14000 / 5 = x2800 magnification.
options.C: Incorrect, this value comes from measuring the wrong structure instead of measuring the scale bar itself.
options.D: Too large, usually from measuring the bar incorrectly or doubling the correct image size.
